name: Jayne Cronlund

bio.statement: Cronlund's voters' pamphlet statement lists a background as nonprofit executive director, school community organizer, family caregiver and AmeriCorps member.
bio.excerpt: Nonprofit executive director, school community organizer, family caregiver, AmeriCorps member

bio.statement: Cronlund's pamphlet statement lists a BA from Temple University and a JD from Northeastern University School of Law.
bio.excerpt: B.A. Temple University; J.D. Northeastern University School of Law

bio.statement: Cronlund's pamphlet statement lists service as 2nd vice president of Southwest Neighborhoods Inc.
OPB reports Cronlund is a nonprofit consultant who led a land conservancy nonprofit for more than a decade.
bio.excerpt: Cronlund is a nonprofit consultant who spent more than a decade leading a land conservancy nonprofit.

positions.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Cronlund says she will use collaboration and shared leadership to solve the city's complex problems.
positions.excerpt: I will use the power of collaboration and shared leadership to solve the complex problems our city faces.

positions.statement: Cronlund's pamphlet statement calls for economic recovery by securing living wage jobs.
positions.excerpt: Economic recovery for our city by securing living wage jobs

positions.statement: Cronlund's pamphlet statement calls for sustained investment in shared spaces such as parks, trails, natural areas and business districts.
positions.excerpt: Sustained investment in safe, shared common spaces like parks, trails, natural areas and business districts.

positions.statement: Cronlund's pamphlet statement says the city faces a mental health and addiction crisis.
positions.excerpt: we are faced with a mental health and addiction crisis

positions.statement: OPB reports Cronlund wants to bolster the city's job market, stabilize its parks system and rebuild public trust in government.
positions.excerpt: She wants to bolster the city’s job market, stabilize the city’s strained parks systems and rebuild public trust in government.

positions.statement: In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Cronlund says charter reform offers a continuing opportunity to restructure how the city does business.
positions.excerpt: Charter reform brings the continuing opportunity to restructure how the city does business

gaps: No voting record (has not held elected office)

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 12 District 4 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form (linked from portland.gov 2026 city candidates page); (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the two articles that profile every District 4 candidate: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 4 council race' (2026-10-07) and Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 4' (2026-09-11). Multi-winner race: OPB states three District 4 seats are on the ballot. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Website discrepancy: the pamphlet statement prints 'jayneforaflourishingfuture.com' while the AUD-120 filing form lists 'jayneforaflourishingportland.com'; the pamphlet version is recorded. Filing form gives occupation 'small business owner, consultant'.
